# Downloading many runs {#sec-at-scale}

For a handful of runs, typing the commands one at a time is fine. For more,
automate it. Pick the route that matches your computer:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  Q{"Where are you running?"} -->|"laptop / any computer"| A["Route A: a simple loop<br/>one run after another"]
  Q -->|"workstation with<br/>many cores"| B["Route B: a few runs<br/>in parallel (xargs -P)"]
  Q -->|"cluster with SLURM"| C["Route C: an array job<br/>(scripts/download_sra.sh)"]
  A & B & C --> S["Same steps per run:<br/>prefetch → vdb-validate → fasterq-dump → compress → clean up"]
```

All three do the same thing for each run:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["one accession"] --> B["prefetch<br/>--max-size u"] --> C["vdb-validate"] --> D["fasterq-dump<br/>--threads N --temp ..."] --> E["pigz / gzip"] --> F["count reads"] --> G["delete .sra<br/>and temp files"]
```

## Route A: a simple loop (any computer)

```bash
cd ~/public_data/GSE52778          # contains SRR_Acc_List.txt
mkdir -p sra tmp fastq
while read -r acc; do
  acc=$(echo "$acc" | tr -d '[:space:]'); [ -z "$acc" ] && continue
  if ls fastq/"$acc"*.fastq.gz >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "have $acc"; continue; fi
  prefetch "$acc" --max-size u -O sra
  vdb-validate "sra/$acc"
  fasterq-dump "sra/$acc" --threads 4 --temp tmp --outdir fastq
  pigz -p 4 fastq/"$acc"*.fastq        # or: gzip fastq/"$acc"*.fastq
  rm -rf "sra/$acc"
done < SRR_Acc_List.txt
```

It skips runs that already have a `.fastq.gz`, so if it stops part-way, run it
again. To keep it running after you close the terminal, start it inside
`screen` or `tmux`, or with `nohup bash download.sh > download.log 2>&1 &`.

## Route B: a few at a time (a workstation)

Save the loop body as a small script that takes one accession, then let
`xargs` run several copies:

```bash
cat > one_run.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
acc=$1; T=${THREADS:-4}
ls fastq/"$acc"*.fastq.gz >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0
prefetch "$acc" --max-size u -O sra
vdb-validate "sra/$acc"
fasterq-dump "sra/$acc" --threads "$T" --temp "tmp/$acc" --outdir fastq
pigz -p "$T" fastq/"$acc"*.fastq
rm -rf "sra/$acc" "tmp/$acc"
EOF
chmod +x one_run.sh
mkdir -p sra tmp fastq
grep . SRR_Acc_List.txt | xargs -n 1 -P 3 ./one_run.sh     # 3 runs at once, 4 threads each
```

`-P 3` runs three downloads at the same time. Make sure you have the disk space
for three conversions at once.

## Route C: an array job on a SLURM cluster

On a cluster, a **SLURM array job** runs one copy of a script per accession,
each as its own job. The repository's
[`scripts/download_sra.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/download_sra.sh)
does this:

```bash
cd /path/to/scratch/GSE52778            # contains SRR_Acc_List.txt
git clone https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data.git
mkdir -p logs
N=$(grep -c . SRR_Acc_List.txt)          # number of non-empty lines
sbatch --array=1-${N}%4 download-public-data/scripts/download_sra.sh SRR_Acc_List.txt fastq
```

- `--array=1-N` runs one task per line; the **`%4`** means at most four at once.
  Keep this low (2–6). Many simultaneous downloads don't go faster, they strain
  the shared filesystem, and NCBI may throttle you.
- `logs/` must exist before you submit; SLURM won't create it.
- The script asks for 6 CPUs, 8 GB memory and 12 hours per run, and uses your
  cluster's **default partition**. To choose one, add `-p <partition>` to the
  `sbatch` command (or an `#SBATCH -p` line to the script).
- **Getting the tools:** if `fasterq-dump` is already on your `PATH` (an
  activated conda environment is inherited by the job), the script uses it.
  Otherwise it tries `module load sra-tools`, then `module load sratoolkit`. If
  your cluster uses another name, set it: `sbatch --export=ALL,SRA_MODULE=<name> ...`.

### Watching it

```bash
squeue -u $USER                                   # tasks show as JOBID_1, JOBID_2, ...
tail logs/sra_download-<JOBID>_3.out              # one task's log
grep -l -i error logs/*.err                       # any task with errors
sacct -j <JOBID> --format=JobID,State,Elapsed,MaxRSS
cat fastq/read_counts.tsv                         # filled in as tasks finish
```

If some tasks fail, fix the cause and submit the same command again. Finished
runs are skipped.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## On UNC Longleaf

Run from your `/work` folder, and add `-p general` to `sbatch` if you want to
name the partition. `module avail sra` shows the toolkit's module name; pass it
with `--export=ALL,SRA_MODULE=<name>` if the script's defaults don't match.
:::

## Other schedulers

PBS/Torque, LSF and SGE all have array jobs too (`qsub -J`, `bsub -J "dl[1-8]"`,
`qsub -t`). The task-number variable differs (`PBS_ARRAY_INDEX`,
`LSB_JOBINDEX`, `SGE_TASK_ID`). Copy `download_sra.sh` and change the `#SBATCH`
lines and the line that reads `SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID`.
